--- title: "Build a design matrix" subtitle: "Model event timing with a typed spec and inspect the regressors." jupyter: python3 --- ## Create events ::: {#49050f09 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import pandas as pd import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import hrf, compile as compile_spec from fmrimod.design_colmap import design_colmap events = pd.DataFrame({ "onset": [0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40], "condition": ["face", "scene", "face", "scene", "face", "scene"], "response_time": [0.8, 1.1, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2], "duration": 2.0, }) events ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
onset condition response_time duration
0 0 face 0.8 2.0
1 8 scene 1.1 2.0
2 16 face 0.7 2.0
3 24 scene 0.9 2.0
4 32 face 1.0 2.0
5 40 scene 1.2 2.0
``` ::: ::: ## Define the acquisition grid ::: {#24086e35 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} sf = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=60, TR=1.0) sf.samples[:8] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` array([0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5]) ``` ::: ::: ## Compile the design `compile()` combines the specification, event table, and acquisition times into an `EventModel` and a baseline model. It returns the design matrix and column metadata without fitting any data. ::: {#f8160466 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} spec = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1") event_model, baseline_model = compile_spec(spec, data=events, sampling_frame=sf) event_model.design_matrix.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (60, 2) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#58a9bcea .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} event_model.column_names ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['condition_condition.face', 'condition_condition.scene'] ``` ::: ::: ## Plot the compiled columns The design heatmap shows the actual regressors used by the model. Compare its bands with the event table before fitting any data. ::: {#3e72f063 .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='6' execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} from fmrimod.visualization import design_map fig = design_map(event_model, figsize=(6, 5), scale="none", title="") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The compiled event design. Color encodes regressor amplitude; it does not show an estimated BOLD effect.](design-matrices_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=677 height=565 fig-alt='Heatmap of the face and scene event regressors across sixty acquisition samples, with alternating response bands.'} ::: ::: ## Inspect column metadata `design_colmap` reports the provenance of every column — which condition, which basis, what role — for the compiled event model. ::: {#d8c9ad2d .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} design_colmap(event_model)[["col", "name", "condition", "role", "basis_name"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
col name condition role basis_name
0 1 condition_condition.face condition.face task spmg1
1 2 condition_condition.scene condition.scene task spmg1
``` ::: ::: ## Add a parametric modulator To model a condition modulated by a trial-by-trial continuous variable (reaction time, accuracy, confidence, ...), use the typed-spec `modulators=` keyword. This expands the term into an unmodulated boxcar plus one regressor per modulator for each condition. By default, modulator values are mean-centered before convolution. This sets the unmodulated effect's reference at the mean modulator value; it does not guarantee orthogonal design columns after convolution. ::: {#44b08fb7 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} modulated_spec = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1", modulators=("response_time",)) mod_model, _ = compile_spec(modulated_spec, data=events, sampling_frame=sf) design_colmap(mod_model)[["col", "name", "condition", "role", "basis_name"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
col name condition role basis_name
0 1 condition_condition.face condition.face task spmg1
1 2 condition_condition.scene condition.scene task spmg1
2 3 condition_response_time_condition:response_time_1 condition:response_time_1 task spmg1
3 4 condition_response_time_condition:response_time_2 condition:response_time_2 task spmg1
``` ::: ::: The added `response_time` regressors appear as their own columns, tagged with where they came from. Because the modulator is part of the typed term metadata rather than a formula-string suffix, you can read off exactly which column belongs to which term before fitting anything. To see a design like this carried through `fmri_lm`, a contrast, and into a group analysis, follow the **[golden path](golden-path.qmd)**. See the [parametric modulators](parametric-modulators.qmd) tutorial for the full story on centering semantics, the `center_modulators=` opt-out, and why fmrimod does not orthogonalize modulators automatically. ## Next - [The golden path](golden-path.qmd) — the whole workflow into group, with a parity check - [Linear model](linear-model.qmd) - [Contrasts](contrasts.qmd) - [Overview and workflow](overview-workflow.qmd)
